title: 538. Horror in the Congo: The Nightmare Begins  (Part 1)

sentences.en: When I was a little chap, I had a passion for maps.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个小男孩的时候，我非常迷恋地图。

sentences.en: I would look for hours at South America or Africa or Australia and lose myself in all the glories of exploration.
sentences.zh: 我会花上好几个小时看着南美洲、非洲或澳大利亚，沉浸在探索的种种荣耀之中。

sentences.en: At that time, there were many blank spaces on the earth, and when I saw one that looked particularly inviting on a map,
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，地球上有许多空白区域，每当我在地图上看到一个看起来特别诱人的地方，

sentences.en: I would put my finger on it and say, when I grow up, I will go there.
sentences.zh: 我就会把手指放在上面说，等我长大了，我要去那里。

sentences.en: There was one, the biggest, the most blank, so to speak, that I had a hankering after.
sentences.zh: 有一个地方，可以说是最大、最空白的地方，让我心向往之。

sentences.en: It had got filled since my boyhood with rivers and lakes and names.
sentences.zh: 自我童年以来，它已经被河流、湖泊和地名填满了。

sentences.en: It had ceased to be a blank space of delightful mystery, a white patch for a boy to dream gloriously over.
sentences.zh: 它不再是一个充满美妙神秘感的空白地带，不再是供一个小男孩做着辉煌美梦的白色色块。

sentences.en: It had become a place of darkness.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一个黑暗的地方。

sentences.en: But there was in it one river especially, a mighty big river, that you could see on the map,
sentences.zh: 但在它之中有一条特别的河流，一条巨大无比的河流，你在地图上就能看到，

sentences.en: resembling an immense snake uncoiled, with its head in the sea, its body at rest, curving afar over a vast country, and its tail lost in the depths of the land.
sentences.zh: 它像一条解开盘绕的巨蛇，蛇头在海里，蛇身静止，在广袤的大地上蜿蜒远去，蛇尾则消失在陆地的深处。

sentences.en: Dash it all, I thought to myself.
sentences.zh: 真见鬼，我心想。

sentences.en: They can't trade without using some kind of craft on that lot of fresh water.
sentences.zh: 他们若不在那片淡水上使用某种船只，根本无法进行贸易。

sentences.en: Steamboats.
sentences.zh: 汽船。

sentences.en: Why shouldn't I try to take charge of one?
sentences.zh: 我为什么不尝试去掌管一艘呢？

sentences.en: I went on along Fleet Street, but could not shake off the idea.
sentences.zh: 我继续沿着弗利特街走着，却怎么也甩不掉这个想法。

sentences.en: The snake had charmed me.
sentences.zh: 这条蛇把我迷住了。

sentences.en: So that is Marlowe, the hero and narrator of Joseph Conrad's novella, Heart of Darkness, which was first published in Blackwood's magazine in 1899.
sentences.zh: 这就是马洛，约瑟夫·康拉德的中篇小说《黑暗的心》中的英雄和叙述者，该小说于1899年首次发表在《布莱克伍德杂志》上。

sentences.en: It famously provided the inspiration for Apocalypse Now, about the American experience in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 它最著名的是为关于美国在越战经历的电影《现代启示录》提供了灵感。

sentences.en: But it was originally written about the European colonial experience in Africa,
sentences.zh: 但它最初是关于欧洲在非洲的殖民经历的，

sentences.en: probably the greatest, the most influential, possibly the most controversial book about that ever written, about the moral dangers of colonialism,
sentences.zh: 这可能是关于该主题写得最伟大、最具影响力、或许也是最具争议的书籍，讲述了殖民主义的道德危险，

sentences.en: and also about the sense of the darkness that lurks in the heart of the human soul, because the darkness in that title, Heart of Darkness, has many different levels.
sentences.zh: 也讲述了潜伏在人类灵魂深处的黑暗感，因为《黑暗的心》这个书名中的黑暗有着许多不同的层面。

sentences.en: There's also the darkness that is London.
sentences.zh: 还有伦敦本身的黑暗。

sentences.en: So Marlowe is talking about this on a boat on the River Thames, narrating it to three friends.
sentences.zh: 所以马洛是在泰晤士河的一艘船上谈论这件事，向三个朋友讲述的。

sentences.en: So the sense that the darkness in Africa is reflecting the darkness in the heart of the European is kind of at the heart of the idea of the book, isn't it, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 因此，非洲的黑暗反映了欧洲人心灵深处的黑暗，这种感觉可以说是这本书的核心思想，对吧，多米尼克？

sentences.en: It is indeed, Tom.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And we'll get on to Heart of Darkness next week, because we'll do an episode about Joseph Conrad and about this book,
sentences.zh: 我们将在下周继续探讨《黑暗的心》，因为我们将做一个关于约瑟夫·康拉德和这本书的节目，

sentences.en: which is one of the most influential books, I would argue, of the modern age.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是现代最具影响力的书籍之一。

sentences.en: And it's a book that I think anticipates so much of the culture of the 20th century and wrestling with kind of man's capacity for evil
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这本书预示了20世纪的大部分文化，并探讨了人类对邪恶的承受力，

sentences.en: and the possibilities of violence and brutality that have been opened up by kind of globalization and by history.
sentences.zh: 以及全球化和历史所释放出的暴力和残酷的可能性。

sentences.en: And so we'll get on to that next week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们下周会继续讨论这个话题。

sentences.en: It's a book rooted in Conrad's own experience.
sentences.zh: 这本书植根于康拉德自己的亲身经历。

sentences.en: So just to give people a sense, he had visited a specific place, a specific point of time.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，他曾访问过一个特定的地方，在特定的时间点。

sentences.en: That place is the Congo Free State under the rule of King Leopold II of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 那个地方就是比利时国王利奥波德二世统治下的刚果自由邦。

sentences.en: Conrad had visited it nine years before he wrote the book as a merchant seaman steering a boat, as Marlow does, into the heart of Africa.
sentences.zh: 康拉德在写这本书的九年前曾访问过那里，当时他是一名商船海员，像马洛一样驾驶着船只驶入非洲腹地。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about his experience, as I said, next week.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们将在下周讨论他的经历。

sentences.en: But this week, we're going to look at the real history that underpins that story.
sentences.zh: 但本周，我们将探讨支撑那个故事的真实历史。

sentences.en: So the story of the Congo Free State, probably the darkest stain in the history of European colonialism, what Conrad himself called, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 刚果自由邦的故事，可以说是欧洲殖民主义历史上最黑暗的污点，康拉德自己曾称其为——我引用一下——

sentences.en: the vilest scramble for loot that ever disfigured the history of human conscience.
sentences.zh: 人类良知历史上遭到的最卑劣的战利品争夺战。

sentences.en: So to give people a sense, we are in Central Africa, between 1885 and 1908.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，我们正处于1885年至1908年的中非。

sentences.en: It's the country that is now known as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, an enormous country, a country that is as big as Britain, France, Germany,
sentences.zh: 这个国家现在被称为刚果民主共和国，是一个巨大的国家，它的面积与英国、法国、德国、

sentences.en: Italy and Spain put together.
sentences.zh: 意大利和西班牙加起来一样大。

sentences.en: Indeed, it's as big as the entire United States, east of the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它和密西西比河以东的整个美国一样大。

sentences.en: And it's actually largely unknown outside its own borders, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 而且它在国境之外基本上鲜为人知，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I guess people have a vague sense of Congo because it became Zaire under President Mobutu, who was kind of the archetype of the kleptocratic African strongman.
sentences.zh: 我想人们对刚果有一个模糊的概念，因为它在莫博图总统统治下变成了扎伊尔，莫博图可以说是克里夫托统治（盗贼统治）下的非洲强人的原型。

sentences.en: And yet there's a sense that no one was quite as kleptocratic or brutal, actually, as Leopold II.
sentences.zh: 然而人们觉得，实际上没有任何人能像利奥波德二世那样腐败贪婪或残酷。

sentences.en: And there's a case for saying that he is the model for much that goes wrong with Africa in the wake of independence, wouldn't you say?
sentences.zh: 有观点认为他是独立后非洲诸多问题的样板，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I would, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我的确这么认为。

sentences.en: I would.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think lots of people would say that this is a kind of foundational moment for the Congo from which nothing ever goes right thereafter.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人会说，这是刚果的一个奠基时刻，从此以后一切都走向了错误的方向。

sentences.en: In that 23-year period when King Leopold is in charge of the Congo, there's a fair claim that it's one of the worst places to live that has ever existed.
sentences.zh: 在利奥波德国王统治刚果的这23年里，有一个合理的说法是，这是有史以来最糟糕的居住地之一。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant book on this called King Leopold's Ghost by the American writer Adam Hochschild.
sentences.zh: 美国作家亚当·霍克希尔德写过一本精彩的书，名为《利奥波德国王的鬼魂》。

sentences.en: We'll be borrowing from that book very liberally.
sentences.zh: 我们将大量借鉴那本书的内容。

sentences.en: So a big shout out to Adam Hochschild's book at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以在节目开头向亚当·霍克希尔德的书致以崇高的敬意。

sentences.en: Not an uncontroversial book itself.
sentences.zh: 这本书本身也并非没有争议。

sentences.en: And in next week's bonus episode, we'll talk about some of the arguments about that book.
sentences.zh: 在下周的特别节目中，我们将讨论关于这本书的一些争论。

sentences.en: But anyway, in King Leopold's Ghost, he says this is one of the great mass killings in human history.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，在《利奥波德国王的鬼魂》中，他指出这是人类历史上最重大的一次大屠杀。

sentences.en: A death toll, he says, of Holocaust dimensions.
sentences.zh: 他说，死亡人数达到了大屠杀的规模。

sentences.en: Exactly how many people die in the Congo Free State is disputed.
sentences.zh: 刚果自由邦究竟死了多少人，目前尚存争议。

sentences.en: But it's millions, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那是数以百万计的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's millions.
sentences.zh: 是数以百万计的。

sentences.en: It's almost certainly millions.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定是数百万。

sentences.en: And some estimates would go as high as 10 million.
sentences.zh: 有些估计甚至高达1000万。

sentences.en: It's not just a story about horror.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个关于恐怖的故事。

sentences.en: It's a story about celebrity, about international relations, royalty.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于名人、国际关系和皇室的故事。

sentences.en: There's a lot of sex in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多香艳的内容。

sentences.en: There's loads of politics.
sentences.zh: 有大量的政治斗争。

sentences.en: It's a story about modernity as well, because this is a new age.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个关于现代性的故事，因为这是一个新时代。

sentences.en: It's the age of the camera.
sentences.zh: 这是相机的时代。

sentences.en: So lots of photography.
sentences.zh: 所以有大量的摄影作品。

sentences.en: Photography is really important.
sentences.zh: 摄影真的非常重要。

sentences.en: Newspapers, telegraphs, and so on.
sentences.zh: 报纸、电报等等。

sentences.en: And actually, as we'll get into in our third episode, it proves the provocation, the cause, for one of the great human rights campaigns in all history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们将在第三集里讲到的那样，它引发并促成了历史上最伟大的人权运动之一。

sentences.en: Arguably the foundational human rights campaign of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 可以说是20世纪奠基性的人权运动。

sentences.en: Yeah, you say of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说是20世纪的。

sentences.en: I mean, it joins the abolitionist movement of the late 18th and early 19th century, which gets rid of slavery, with the human rights movements of the late 20th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它将18世纪末和19世纪初废除奴隶制的废奴运动，与20世纪末的人权运动联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that it's very, very Anglophone, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它是非常非常讲英语的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's very centred in Britain and in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它高度集中在英国和美国。

sentences.en: And again, Britain's role in all this is really, really intriguing.
sentences.zh: 同样，英国在这一切中所扮演的角色真的非常非常耐人寻味。

sentences.en: It's quite, I mean, intriguingly ambivalent, really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上相当耐人寻味地充满矛盾。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So it definitely merits a series.
sentences.zh: 所以它绝对值得做一个系列节目。

sentences.en: And like all good series, it needs a riveting central character.
sentences.zh: 像所有优秀的长篇节目一样，它需要一个引人入胜的核心人物。

sentences.en: In this case, a villain.
sentences.zh: 在这个案子里，是一个恶棍。

sentences.en: And history has absolutely provided us with one.
sentences.zh: 而历史绝对为我们提供了一个。

sentences.en: And this is King Leopold II of Belgium, who Hochschild says is as interesting, as multi-layered, as greedy, as cunning, as charming,
sentences.zh: 这就是比利时国王利奥波德二世，霍克希尔德称他与莎士比亚笔下的任何反派一样有趣、多面、贪婪、狡猾、迷人

sentences.en: and as untrustworthy as any of Shakespeare's villains.
sentences.zh: 且不可信。

sentences.en: And if he is the villain, the great irony is he never, ever sets foot in the Congo.
sentences.zh: 如果他是那个恶棍，最大的讽刺是他从未踏足过刚果半步。

sentences.en: He never lays eyes on the Congo.
sentences.zh: 他从未亲眼见过刚果。

sentences.en: His villainy, as it were, is carried out from afar, which makes him a very 20th century figure.
sentences.zh: 他的恶行可以说是在远方实施的，这使他成为一个非常具有20世纪特色的人物。

sentences.en: You think of all these dictators who kill so many millions of people without ever shedding blood themselves.
sentences.zh: 你会想到所有这些独裁者，他们自己从不沾血却杀害了数以百万计的人。

sentences.en: But also, you could say, if you were an anti-capitalist, that he's kind of the exemplification of great corporations now, who leech money from distant parts of the world,
sentences.zh: 但你也可以说，如果你是一个反资本主义者，他某种程度上就是现代大企业的典范，从世界各地遥远的角落吸取金钱，

sentences.en: rely on products made by slave labour.
sentences.zh: 依赖奴隶劳工制造的产品。

sentences.en: Leopold is kind of the archetype of that as well, wouldn't you say?
sentences.zh: 利奥波德某种程度上也是这种现象的原型，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: He is indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we'll absolutely get into that.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对会深入探讨这一点。

sentences.en: This is the classic example, you might say, of the rapacity of corporate capitalism carried to its ultimate murderous extreme.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，这是公司资本主义的贪婪被推向其最终的谋杀极端的经典例子。

sentences.en: But let's start with Leopold himself.
sentences.zh: 但让我们从利奥波德本人开始讲起。

sentences.en: So he was born in 1835, when Belgium had been independent from the Netherlands for five years.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1835年，当时比利时从荷兰独立已经五年了。

sentences.en: So he's the son of the very first king of the Belgians, who's also called Leopold.
sentences.zh: 所以他是比利时第一位国王的儿子，这位国王也叫利奥波德。

sentences.en: He's brought up at a castle called Lacken, which is outside Brussels, where he spends most of his time.
sentences.zh: 他在布鲁塞尔郊外一座名为拉肯的城堡长大，他大部分时间都在那里度过。

sentences.en: He speaks French and German and English, not interestingly Flemish, which is the language of most of his subjects.
sentences.zh: 他说法语、德语和英语，有趣的是不说佛兰德语，而那是他大部分臣民的语言。

sentences.en: Now, Leopold's parents, Leopold and Louise, had a pretty miserable, loveless marriage.
sentences.zh: 现在，利奥波德的父母，利奥波德和路易丝，有着相当悲惨且毫无爱意的婚姻。

sentences.en: And they treated their son very, very coldly.
sentences.zh: 他们对儿子的态度非常非常冷淡。

sentences.en: So if he wanted to talk to his father, he had to apply through a secretary for an audience.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他想和父亲说话，他必须通过秘书申请觐见。

sentences.en: And when his father wants to tell his son something, he got a secretary to do it for him.
sentences.zh: 当他父亲想告诉儿子什么事情时，他会找个秘书代劳。

sentences.en: To be fair, that is how I communicate with Katie and Eliza.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，这就是我与凯蒂和伊丽莎交流的方式。

sentences.en: So you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以你知道吗？

sentences.en: When I was reading this, the parallels between you and King Leopold were leaping off the page.
sentences.zh: 当我读到这里时，你和利奥波德国王之间的相似之处简直跃然纸上。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: So, yeah, what is it about me and 20th century monarchs?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我跟20世纪的君主有什么渊源吗？

sentences.en: The Kaiser, Leopold II?
sentences.zh: 威廉二世，利奥波德二世？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's chilling.
sentences.zh: 是的，令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: So Leopold, maybe this will ring a bell with you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以利奥波德，这可能会让你深有同感，汤姆。

sentences.en: He grows up a moody, kind of gangling and humorless boy.
sentences.zh: 他长大后成了一个喜怒无常、身材高瘦且毫无幽默感的男孩。

sentences.en: That's me.
sentences.zh: 那不就是我吗。

sentences.en: But the thing is, even at the time, his father says of him, he's very cunning.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，即使在当时，他的父亲也评价他说，他非常狡猾。

sentences.en: His father compares him with a fox.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲把他比作一只狐狸。

sentences.en: Says Leopold is like a fox.
sentences.zh: 说利奥波德就像一只狐狸。

sentences.en: He slowly and stealthily picks out his path.
sentences.zh: 他缓慢而隐秘地选择自己的道路。

sentences.en: Stalks the chickens.
sentences.zh: 悄悄接近鸡群。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没，错。

sentences.en: And then he makes his move.
sentences.zh: 然后他采取行动。

sentences.en: So by the 1850s, Leopold is in his teens.
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪50年代，利奥波德正处于青少年时期。

sentences.en: He's become, I think it's fair to say, an extremely awkward and unattractive young man.
sentences.zh: 可以公平地说，他已经变成了一个极其笨拙且毫无吸引力的年轻男子。

sentences.en: People always comment on how unbelievably tall he is.
sentences.zh: 人们总是评论他高得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: He's a bit like Baron Trump.
sentences.zh: 他有点像巴伦·特朗普。

sentences.en: He's massively tall and awkward looking.
sentences.zh: 他身材魁梧奇高，看起来很笨拙。

sentences.en: But with less knowledge of crypto, presumably.
sentences.zh: 不过据推测他对加密货币的了解要少得多。

sentences.en: Presumably, yes.
sentences.zh: 据推测是这样的。

sentences.en: He's got an enormous beard and everybody comments on his absolutely enormous nose.
sentences.zh: 他留着一把巨大的胡子，每个人都对他的超大鼻子议论纷纷。

sentences.en: So Disraeli said of it, it's such a nose as a young prince has in a fairy tale, thanks to the intervention of a malignant fairy.
sentences.zh: 所以迪斯雷利这样评价它：这是一个童话里年轻王子才有的鼻子，多亏了一个恶毒仙子的干预。

sentences.en: So he's not a looker, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 所以公平地说，他长得不好看。

sentences.en: And he's very, very charmless.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常非常没有魅力。

sentences.en: So, you know, he has to compensate for that with his cunning.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他必须用他的狡猾来弥补这一点。

sentences.en: When he's 18 years old, his father takes him to Vienna to get a Habsburg bride.
sentences.zh: 在他18岁的时候，他父亲带他去维也纳寻找一位哈布斯堡王朝的新娘。

sentences.en: And this is a 16-year-old called Archduchess Marie Henriette.
sentences.zh: 这是一位16岁的少女，名叫玛丽·亨利埃特女大公。

sentences.en: And she's great.
sentences.zh: 她很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's like the Emperor Claudius and Carmen Harris, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 她就像克劳狄乌斯皇帝和卡门·哈里斯，对吧？

sentences.en: She has a tremendous braying laugh.
sentences.zh: 她有一种极其刺耳的驴叫般的笑声。

sentences.en: Yes, she does.
sentences.zh: 是的，她确实有。

sentences.en: She's got a great laugh.
sentences.zh: 她笑起来很豪爽。

sentences.en: That echoes around Belgium.
sentences.zh: 那笑声在比利时回荡。

sentences.en: And she loves laughing.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢笑。

sentences.en: She loves laughing.
sentences.zh: 她太喜欢笑了。

sentences.en: And Leopold is shocked by this because he hates laughing.
sentences.zh: 而利奥波德对此感到震惊，因为他讨厌笑。

sentences.en: They go to Venice on holiday and he behaves really coldly to her.
sentences.zh: 他们去威尼斯度假，他对她表现得非常冷淡。

sentences.en: He won't let it go on a gondola that she's booked and all this.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不肯让她坐她预定的贡多拉，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And she bursts into tears.
sentences.zh: 而她突然泪流满面。

sentences.en: And people see this in public.
sentences.zh: 人们在公众场合看到了这一幕。

sentences.en: They say, oh, dude, this is an all-starred marriage.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，老兄，这是一场明星般的婚姻。

sentences.en: And a month after they got married, she tells one of her friends, if God hears my prayers, I shan't go on living much longer.
sentences.zh: 就在他们结婚一个月后，她对一个朋友说，如果上帝听到我的祈祷，我将不久于人世。

sentences.en: That's not what you want to hear after honeymoon.
sentences.zh: 蜜月过后可不想听到这种话。

sentences.en: So, so much of Leopold's colonial ambitions, there is an argument that basically it stems from his own insecurity and misery, that it's a massive kind of displacement exercise.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于利奥波德的殖民野心，有一种观点认为，它基本上源于他自身的安全感缺失和痛苦，这是一种巨大的情感转移运动。

sentences.en: Anyway, he doesn't actually become king of Belgium until 1865.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他直到1865年才真正成为比利时国王。

sentences.en: So he spends a lot of time waiting for his father to die.
sentences.zh: 所以他花了大量时间等待父亲去世。

sentences.en: And while he's doing that, he has this kind of gnawing insecurity that he's going to be inheriting a country that is just a sort of pathetic minnow on the world stage.
sentences.zh: 而在他这样做的时候，他有一种挥之不去的不安全感，觉得自己将要继承的国家只是世界舞台上一个可悲的小不点。

sentences.en: Of course, Belgium is kind of squashed between France and an increasingly unified Germany.
sentences.zh: 当然，比利时就像是被夹在法国和一个日益统一的德国之间。

sentences.en: And Leopold feels this very keenly.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德对此有着非常深切的感受。

sentences.en: He says of Belgium, petit pays, petit gens, little country, little people.
sentences.zh: 他这样形容比利时：小国家，小人物。

sentences.en: And he thinks, you know, I deserve better than the Belgian people.
sentences.zh: 他心想，你知道的，我值得拥有比比利时人民更好的东西。

sentences.en: And what he really wants is an empire.
sentences.zh: 他真正想要的是一个帝国。

sentences.en: He wants colonies.
sentences.zh: 他想要殖民地。

sentences.en: And he's very aggrieved that he's inheriting a kingdom that doesn't have any.
sentences.zh: 他为自己继承了一个没有殖民地的王国而感到非常委屈。

sentences.en: Three years before he becomes king of the Belgians, he goes on holiday to Spain and he goes to
sentences.zh: 在他成为比利时国王的三年前，他去西班牙度假，去了

sentences.en: Seville and he spends his time in Seville.
sentences.zh: 塞维利亚，他在塞维利亚度过了一段时间。

sentences.en: He spends weeks at the great archive of the Indies going through the records, looking at just how much money Spain had made from its colonies.
sentences.zh: 他在伟大的印第安档案馆花了几个星期翻阅记录，查看西班牙从其殖民地赚取了多少财富。

sentences.en: So this is the 16th century, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这是16世纪，对吧？

sentences.en: The conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 征服者们。

sentences.en: The conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 征服者们。

sentences.en: How much money they had made from the territories they exploited.
sentences.zh: 他们从剥削的领土中赚取了多少钱。

sentences.en: And this fires his imagination.
sentences.zh: 这激发了他的想象力。

sentences.en: He makes trips to Ceylon and to Burma to see how the British make money from their colonies.
sentences.zh: 他前往锡兰和缅甸，看看英国人是如何从他们的殖民地赚钱的。

sentences.en: He reads a book called Java or How to Manage a Colony, which is all about the Dutch in the
sentences.zh: 他读了一本书叫《爪哇或如何管理殖民地》，这本书讲的全是荷兰人在

sentences.en: East Indies.
sentences.zh: 东印度群岛的事。

sentences.en: And this is written unbelievably.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，这本书是这个人写的。

sentences.en: You've seen the bloke who wrote this book?
sentences.zh: 你见过写这本书的家伙吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, very funny.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常有趣。

sentences.en: J.W.B.
sentences.zh: J.W.B.

sentences.en: Money.
sentences.zh: 莫尼。

sentences.en: You see, if he ran a bank, I'd very happily advertise his bank on the rest of the system.
sentences.zh: 你看，如果他经营一家银行，我会非常乐意在系统的其他地方帮他的银行做广告。

sentences.en: Would you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: J.W.B.
sentences.zh: J.W.B.

sentences.en: Money Bank.
sentences.zh: 莫尼银行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So invest your money in it.
sentences.zh: 所以把钱投资在里面吧。

sentences.en: Well, you should advertise his book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你应该帮他的书做广告。

sentences.en: Money's book is all about how you get a colony to turn a profit.
sentences.zh: 莫尼的书讲的全是如何让殖民地实现盈利。

sentences.en: You see, that's what Leopold is interested in.
sentences.zh: 你看，这正是利奥波德感兴趣的地方。

sentences.en: Even more than the prestige and certainly a lot more than any possible civilizing mission aspect of colonialism.
sentences.zh: 比起声望，甚至比起殖民主义任何可能的文明化使命，他更在乎这个。

sentences.en: What he cares about is cash.
sentences.zh: 他在乎的是现金。

sentences.en: And in this book, J.W.B.
sentences.zh: 而在这本书中，J.W.B.

sentences.en: Money says the Dutch have turned a profit from Java by using forced labor to have plantations and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 莫尼说，荷兰人通过利用强迫劳动力经营种植园以及诸如此类的事情，从爪哇获得了利润。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the fact that it's Dutch colonies, I mean, that must really irritate him.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，既然是荷兰的殖民地，我的意思是，这一定很惹恼他。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The great rivals.
sentences.zh: 死对头。

sentences.en: The great rivals.
sentences.zh: 死对头。

sentences.en: I mean, even more than the Germans or the French having colonies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，甚至比德国人或法国人拥有殖民地更让他生气。

sentences.en: The Dutch.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人。

sentences.en: Awful.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: So he looks at the Dutch and he says, yeah, they're very unsentimental.
sentences.zh: 所以他看着荷兰人说，是的，他们非常冷酷无情。

sentences.en: They've used forced labor.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了强迫劳动力。

sentences.en: And it is clear, he writes, the only way to civilize and uplift these indolent and corrupt peoples is basically by forcing them to work so that we can make money.
sentences.zh: 他写道，很显然，要使这些懒散腐败的人民文明并振作起来，唯一的办法基本上就是强迫他们劳动，这样我们才能赚钱。

sentences.en: So here's the great paradox.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是最大的矛盾所在。

sentences.en: Other Belgians don't really care about colonists.
sentences.zh: 其他比利时人并不真正在乎殖民者。

sentences.en: They are very conscious they're only a small and newly independent country.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚自己只是一个弱小且刚独立不久的国家。

sentences.en: They don't even really have a merchant navy of their own.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有真正属于自己的商船队。

sentences.en: So how could they possibly maintain a colonial empire?
sentences.zh: 所以他们怎么可能维持一个殖民帝国呢？

sentences.en: But for Leopold, all of his misery, all of his loneliness and awkwardness, I think he has poured into this great project of acquiring colonists.
sentences.zh: 但对利奥波德来说，我想他把自己的所有痛苦、所有孤独和笨拙，都倾注在了这个获取殖民地的伟大计划中。

sentences.en: And he believes this is the only thing that will make him happy.
sentences.zh: 他相信这是唯一能让他快乐的事情。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: That geography apparently was his only subject that he was interested in as a boy.
sentences.zh: 据说地理是他小时候唯一感兴趣的科目。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit like Marlow at the beginning of this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像本集开头的马洛。

sentences.en: This idea of looking at the world and Marlow dreams of going on adventures there.
sentences.zh: 这种审视世界的想法，马洛梦想着去那里经历冒险。

sentences.en: And Leopold dreams of basically grabbing bits of it and using it to make money.
sentences.zh: 而利奥波德梦想着基本上抢占它的一部分并用它来赚钱。

sentences.en: He absolutely does indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实完全是这样的。

sentences.en: He reminds me, reading the book by Adam Hochschild, I was reminded of Scrooge.
sentences.zh: 读亚当·霍克希尔德的书时，这让我想起了吝啬鬼斯克鲁奇。

sentences.en: So Scrooge who, you know, deep down what Scrooge wants, Scrooge wants love.
sentences.zh: 所以斯克鲁奇，你知道的，斯克鲁奇内心深处真正想要的是爱。

sentences.en: And he's become a miser and a terrible person.
sentences.zh: 而他却变成了一个守财奴和一个可怕的人。

sentences.en: You are a sentimentaliSt.
sentences.zh: 你真是个感伤主义者。

sentences.en: Well, no, I don't think you can be sentimental about King Leopold II, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，我认为正如我们将看到的，你不可能对利奥波德二世国王心存感伤。

sentences.en: But you're saying that all the horrors of the Congo is because he didn't have love as a child.
sentences.zh: 但你是说刚果的所有恐怖行径都是因为他童年缺乏爱。

sentences.en: I think his loveless life and his obsessiveness, he's not just an ordinary colonialist, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 我认为他那没有爱的一生和他的偏执，正如我们所看到的，他不仅仅是一个普通的殖民主义者。

sentences.en: There is something really weirdly obsessive about him.
sentences.zh: 他身上有一种非常诡异的偏执。

sentences.en: And I wonder how much of that, I mean, also the way he behaves, the stuff with, as we will see, his obsession with hygiene is very, very peculiar.
sentences.zh: 我在想这其中有多少，我的意思是，还有他的行为方式，正如我们将看到的，他对卫生的痴迷非常非常奇特。

sentences.en: And with very young ladies.
sentences.zh: 而且对非常年轻的女士也是如此。

sentences.en: And with very, very young girls.
sentences.zh: 还有对非常非常年轻的女孩也是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There's a lot of bad things to be said, I think it's fair to say, about King Leopold II.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，关于利奥波德二世国王，有很多不好的事情可以说。

sentences.en: Anyway, 1865, he becomes king at laSt.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，1865年，他终于成为了国王。

sentences.en: Now, for the next 10 years, he doesn't actually manage to get the empire he wants.
sentences.zh: 接下来这10年里，他并没有真正得到他想要的帝国。

sentences.en: He investigates various schemes.
sentences.zh: 他研究了各种计划。

sentences.en: He'd like to buy a bit of Argentina.
sentences.zh: 他想买下阿根廷的一部分。

sentences.en: He'd like to buy a bit of the Nile Delta.
sentences.zh: 他想买下尼罗河三角洲的一部分。

sentences.en: He even talks about acquiring Fiji.
sentences.zh: 他甚至谈到要收购斐济。

sentences.en: But he doesn't really get anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有取得什么实质进展。

sentences.en: But not Greenland.
sentences.zh: 但不是格陵兰岛。

sentences.en: They're not Greenland, no.
sentences.zh: 不是格陵兰岛，没有。

sentences.en: But in 1875, he thinks he might be onto something.
sentences.zh: 但在1875年，他觉得自己可能要有所收获了。

sentences.en: He's offered Spain cash for the Philippines for the second time.
sentences.zh: 他第二次向西班牙提出用现金购买菲律宾。

sentences.en: And to his deep disappointment, they turn him down again.
sentences.zh: 令他深感失望的是，他们再次拒绝了他。

sentences.en: And he says to one of his courtiers, OK, I'm going to have a look at Africa now.
sentences.zh: 他对他的一个朝臣说，好吧，我现在要看看非洲了。

sentences.en: Maybe Africa's the place.
sentences.zh: 也许非洲才是那个地方。

sentences.en: So now at last in this story, we come to Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，在这段故事中，我们终于来到了非洲。

sentences.en: Now, the great scramble for Africa, which people think of as a 19th century thing, is actually really only concentrated in the final decades of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们认为是19世纪之物的疯狂瓜分非洲，实际上真正集中的时期只有19世纪的最后几十年。

sentences.en: So at this point, 1875, it hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 所以在当时，即1875年，这还没有发生。

sentences.en: The French are in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 法国人在阿尔及利亚。

sentences.en: The Portuguese are in what become Mozambique and Angola.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人在后来的莫桑比克和安哥拉。

sentences.en: The British and the Burrs both have footholds in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 英国人和布尔人在南非都有据点。

sentences.en: And various countries have kind of trading ports and enclaves on the coast of West Africa.
sentences.zh: 各种国家在西非海岸都有某种贸易港口和飞地。

sentences.en: But about three quarters of Africa, really meaning the interior, has not yet been penetrated by European empires.
sentences.zh: 但大约四分之三的非洲，实际上是指内陆地区，尚未被欧洲帝国渗透。

sentences.en: For Europeans, the wealth of Africa is associated with the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 对欧洲人来说，非洲的财富与海岸联系在一起。

sentences.en: There's the assumption that there's nothing in the middle that would be worth the effort of colonising.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种假设，认为中间没有任何东西值得花力气去殖民。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: People just think, well, it's just impenetrable jungle.
sentences.zh: 人们只是认为，这只是一片无法穿透的丛林。

sentences.en: What could possibly be there?
sentences.zh: 那里怎么可能会有什么东西？

sentences.en: It's a blank space, as Conrad puts it.
sentences.zh: 正如康拉德所说，这是一片空白。

sentences.en: But by this point, the mid-1870s, Africa is making the news in a way it hasn't ever done before.
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时候，即19世纪70年代中期，非洲开始成为新闻焦点，这是前所未有的。

sentences.en: There have been a series of very eye-catching expeditions.
sentences.zh: 有一系列非常引人注目的探险活动。

sentences.en: And, of course, the most famous one, which lots of listeners will have heard of,
sentences.zh: 当然，最著名的一个，许多听众可能都听说过，

sentences.en: is the expedition by the journalist Henry Morton Stanley to find the missionary David Livingston in modern-day Tanzania in 1871, which was financed by the New York Herald.
sentences.zh: 就是记者亨利·莫顿·斯坦利于1871年在现今的坦桑尼亚寻找传教士大卫·利文斯顿的探险，该探险由《纽约先驱报》资助。

sentences.en: And thanks to these new innovations of cheap newspapers and the Telegraph, Stanley and Livingston become international celebrities far beyond Britain and America.
sentences.zh: 多亏了廉价报纸和电报这些新创新，斯坦利和利文斯顿成为了远超英国和美国的国际名人。

sentences.en: So they're making front-page news in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以他们成为了比利时头版头条的新闻。

sentences.en: And King Leopold, we know, follows the story very closely and actually kept a sort of scrapbook, including handwritten notes that he was making following Stanley's journey.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，利奥波德国王非常密切地关注这个故事，甚至还保留了一种剪贴簿，里面包括他追随斯坦利旅程时做的手写笔记。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, isn't it, because Livingston is all about fighting slavery.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，不是吗？因为利文斯顿所做的一切都是为了反对奴隶制。

sentences.en: His heart is in the right place.
sentences.zh: 他的心是好的。

sentences.en: Stanley, a much more ambivalent figure.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利则是一个更加矛盾的人物。

sentences.en: I mean, he's looking for Livingston, basically, to make a name for himself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他寻找利文斯顿，基本上是为了让自己扬名立万。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: For celebrity and for money are two things which will play a big part in this story.
sentences.zh: 名气和金钱是将在个故事中发挥巨大作用的两件事。

sentences.en: So the question for Leopold is, can he get them?
sentences.zh: 所以对利奥波德来说，问题在于，他能得到这些吗？

sentences.en: He wants a colony that will turn a profit.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个能盈利的殖民地。

sentences.en: Can he make money from Africa?
sentences.zh: 他能从非洲赚钱吗？

sentences.en: And the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: Not through slavery, as you once could, but through something that is extremely fashionable and very lucrative.
sentences.zh: 不是通过曾经那样奴隶制，而是通过一种非常时髦且非常有利可图的方式。

sentences.en: And that something is ivory.
sentences.zh: 而那个东西就是象牙。

sentences.en: Now, the Victorians are obsessed by ivory.
sentences.zh: 现在，维多利亚时代的人对象牙痴迷不已。

sentences.en: It's exotic because, of course, it comes from elephant tusks.
sentences.zh: 它很异国情调，因为当然，它来自象牙。

sentences.en: But it's also unbelievably useful and malleable because it's really, really easy to carve ivory.
sentences.zh: 但它也极其有用且具有可塑性，因为雕刻象牙真的非常非常容易。

sentences.en: So if you went into a sort of genteel Victorian household, anywhere in the Western world, in the 1870s or 1880s, there would be the handles of cutlery.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你走进19世纪70年代或80年代西方世界的任何一个高雅的维多利亚式家庭，你会看到餐具的手柄。

sentences.en: There would be billiard balls.
sentences.zh: 会有台球。

sentences.en: There would be combs, fans.
sentences.zh: 会有梳子、扇子。

sentences.en: There would be brooches.
sentences.zh: 会有胸针。

sentences.en: There would be chess pieces, piano keys, false teeth.
sentences.zh: 会有国际象棋棋子、钢琴键、假牙。

sentences.en: All of these kinds of things are made of ivory.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西都是用象牙做的。

sentences.en: Because Hochschild compares it actually to plastic, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为霍克希尔德实际上把它比作塑料，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's such a kind of useful product, which is brilliant for the Victorians and obviously very bad news for the elephants.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常实用的产品，对维多利亚时代的人来说太棒了，但对大象来说显然是个非常糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And you can make so much money from it.
sentences.zh: 你可以靠它赚大钱。

sentences.en: So two elephant tusks will give you hundreds of piano keys or thousands upon thousands of false teeth.
sentences.zh: 所以两根象牙就能给你提供几百个钢琴键或者成千上万副假牙。

sentences.en: And it sounds comical, but there is an awful lot of money to be made here.
sentences.zh: 听起来很滑稽，但这里确实有大量的钱可赚。

sentences.en: And Stanley, after returning from his expedition, has gone around telling people, my God,
sentences.zh: 斯坦利从探险归来后，到处跟人说，天哪，

sentences.en: there is so much ivory in Equatorial Africa that the people there use it for their doorposts because it's just so plentiful.
sentences.zh: 赤道非洲有那么多的象牙，以至于当地人把它用作门柱，因为实在是太多了。

sentences.en: So it's kind of ivory equivalent of El Dorado.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是黄金国的象牙版。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That sense.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉。

sentences.en: So this is portable wealth.
sentences.zh: 所以这是可携带的财富。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Which is the key to gold in the new world, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 这正是新世界黄金的关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: In the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 在16世纪。

sentences.en: But the difference between the 16th century and now is that to acquire a colony, I think you have to try much harder to present it as part of a civilizing mission.
sentences.zh: 但16世纪与现在的一个区别在于，如果你想获得一块殖民地，我认为你必须付出更多努力，把它包装成一项文明使命的一部分。

sentences.en: So this is the high point of high Victorianism, the belief in kind of moral uplift and Europe's right to the moral leadership of the planet.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是维多利亚时代全盛期的顶峰，人们坚信某种道德提升以及欧洲对地球的道德领导权。

sentences.en: All these things that we may well think of now as being freighted with hypocrisy or of kind of patronizing condescension.
sentences.zh: 所有这些我们现在看来充满伪善或某种居高临下的优越感的事情。

sentences.en: But at the time, people do actually take genuinely seriously.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，人们确实是发自内心地认真对待的。

sentences.en: So Leopold knows that he will have to, I think, tick three boxes if he wants a colony.
sentences.zh: 因此，利奥波德知道，如果他想要一块殖民地，我想他必须达成三个条件。

sentences.en: First of all, he has to present it as a scientific project, an intellectual project.
sentences.zh: 首先，他必须把它包装成一个科学项目、一个知识项目。

sentences.en: So literally filling in those blank spaces, mapping what has previously been unknown.
sentences.zh: 也就是字面意义上填补那些空白，绘制出以前未知事物的地图。

sentences.en: Secondly, I think he has to tick the moral uplift box.
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为他必须达成道德提升这一项。

sentences.en: So he has to say, well, I only want a colony because I want to spread the gospel of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须说，好吧，我想要殖民地只是因为我想传播基督教的福音。

sentences.en: Of course, something that matters tremendously to the Victorians.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对维多利亚时代的人来说至关重要。

sentences.en: But also, Dominic, the spreading of Christianity is also intimately associated with the campaign to abolish slavery.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，传播基督教也与废除奴隶制的运动紧密相连。

sentences.en: Yes, that's the third thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是第三点。

sentences.en: Britain has been leading that campaign since the early 19th century,
sentences.zh: 自19世纪初以来，英国一直在领导这场运动，

sentences.en: and it has provided an absolutely crucial kind of moral justification for what has been a process of expansion of British imperial control.
sentences.zh: 它为英国帝国控制权扩张的过程提供了一种绝对至关重要的道德正当性。

sentences.en: So Livingstone, even though he's not overtly an imperialist,
sentences.zh: 因此，利文斯顿虽然表面上不是一个帝国主义者，

sentences.en: the fact that he is carving out a moral mission for Britain in the middle of Africa is obviously very useful from an imperial point of view.
sentences.zh: 但他为英国在非洲中部开创了一项道德使命，从帝国的角度来看，这显然非常有用。

sentences.en: And I guess that Leopold is, I mean, he reads the Times, doesn't he, every morning?
sentences.zh: 我想利奥波德他，我的意思是，他每天早晨都会读《泰晤士报》，对吧？

sentences.en: He is very alert to the kind of symbiosis between that moral mission to eradicate slavery and imperialism in the British form, and he wants a bit of it.
sentences.zh: 他对那种以英国形式根除奴隶制的道德使命与帝国主义之间的共生关系非常敏锐，他也想分一杯羹。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我想你完全说对了。

sentences.en: I think he absolutely sees what's going on with the other empires.
sentences.zh: 我想他完全看清了其他帝国正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: I think in Leopold's case, what makes him slightly unusual is that all the evidence we have of his letters and so on is that for him, the profit motive is all,
sentences.zh: 我认为在利奥波德的案例中，他有点与众不同的是，我们从他的书信等所有证据中都可以看出，对重利主义他而言就是一切，

sentences.en: and that the rest of it is effectively just a justification for making money.
sentences.zh: 而其余的一切实际上都只是为了赚钱而找的借口。

sentences.en: I mean, he's pretty shameless about that, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这方面他可以说是毫无廉耻。

sentences.en: So this is how he proceeds.
sentences.zh: 这就是他行事的方式。

sentences.en: And I have to say, he's a terrible man, King Leopold, but he really is a cunning and a methodical and a clever man.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，利奥波德国王是个糟糕的家伙，但他确实是一个狡猾、有条理且聪明的人。

sentences.en: A vulpine figure.
sentences.zh: 一个像狐狸一样的人物。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: So his first step is to convene a big geographical conference in Brussels at the end of 1876, and he invites all the big celebrities of the sort of the Africa industry of the day.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的第一步是在1876年底在布鲁塞尔召集一次大型地理会议，他邀请了当时非洲行业的所有大咖名人。

sentences.en: So there are explorers from France and Germany.
sentences.zh: 其中包括来自法国和德国的探险家。

sentences.en: He's got a celebrity explorer called Gerhard Rolfs, who had actually had himself circumcised so that he could pass for a Muslim in the Sahara.
sentences.zh: 他请到了一位名叫格哈德·罗尔夫斯的知名探险家，他实际上为了在撒哈拉沙漠伪装成穆斯林而割过包皮。

sentences.en: So, you know, somebody who had suffered for his queSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个为他的追求吃过苦头的人。

sentences.en: His exploration.
sentences.zh: 他的探险。

sentences.en: His exploration.
sentences.zh: 他的探险。

sentences.en: He's got the president of the British Anti-Slavery Society, Sir Thomas Fowle Buxton.
sentences.zh: 他请来了英国反奴隶制协会主席托马斯·福尔·巴克斯顿爵士。

sentences.en: He's got the president of the Church Missionary Society, Sir John Kenway.
sentences.zh: 他请来了英国圣公会差会主席约翰·肯韦爵士。

sentences.en: He's even got the bloke who used to command the Royal Navy's Indian Ocean Anti-Slavery Squadron.
sentences.zh: 他甚至请来了曾指挥英国皇家海军印度洋反奴隶制中队的那个家伙。

sentences.en: So he is ticking all of those boxes.
sentences.zh: 因此，他把这些条件全部满足了。

sentences.en: He's inviting a lot of people who are genuinely animated by what we might call humanitarian as well as imperialistic concerns.
sentences.zh: 他邀请了许多真正被我们所谓的出于人道主义以及帝国主义关切所驱使的人。

sentences.en: And he welcomes them and he says, you know, I dream of a crusade worthy of this century of progress to open to civilization,
sentences.zh: 他欢迎他们并说道，你知道，我梦想着进行一场无愧于这个进步世纪的十字军东征，去开拓文明，

sentences.en: the only part of our globe which it has not yet penetrated, to pierce the darkness which hangs over entire peoples.
sentences.zh: 去开拓我们地球上唯一尚未涉足的部分，去穿透笼罩着整个人群的黑暗。

sentences.en: That word darkness again, which is going to come up throughout this series.
sentences.zh: 又是“黑暗”这个词，它将在整个系列中不断出现。

sentences.en: And he says to them, don't think that I want anything for myself, he says.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，不要以为我为自己谋求任何东西，他说。

sentences.en: I have no ambition other than to serve Belgium.
sentences.zh: 我除了为比利时服务，没有别的野心。

sentences.en: Now, that, as we've seen, is a lie.
sentences.zh: 现在，正如我们所见，这是一个谎言。

sentences.en: He despises Belgium.
sentences.zh: 他鄙视比利时。

sentences.en: And he, as we will also see, he doesn't want to serve Belgium at all.
sentences.zh: 正如我们也将看到的，他根本不想为比利时服务。

sentences.en: He only wants to serve himself.
sentences.zh: 他只想为自己服务。

sentences.en: And he says to them, look, I've assembled you because I think it would be nice for us to identify places in the blank spaces of Africa, which could be bases,
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，看哪，我把大家召集起来，是因为我觉得我们有必要找出非洲空白地带中可以作为基地的地方，

sentences.en: which could be kind of, they could be hospitals, they could be scientific research centers, they could be trading stations.
sentences.zh: 它们可以成为某种，可以成为医院，可以成为科学研究中心，可以成为贸易站。

sentences.en: With an emphasis on the trading.
sentences.zh: 重点在于贸易。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: And these will be run.
sentences.zh: 这些将由人来运营。

sentences.en: I don't want to, I mean, Belgium won't run them, right?
sentences.zh: 我不想，我的意思是，比利时不会去运营它们，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we don't want to, we absolutely, the last thing we'd want is a colony.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不想，绝对不想，最不需要的就是殖民地。

sentences.en: He says, we'll set up an international African association.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们将成立一个国际非洲协会。

sentences.en: And it'll be based, why not base it in Brussels, actually?
sentences.zh: 它的总部将设在——为什么不干脆设在布鲁塞尔呢？

sentences.en: And for its first chairman, I mean, if no one else wants to do it, I'd very happily put myself forward.
sentences.zh: 至于它的第一任主席，我的意思是，如果没有其他人想干，我非常乐意毛遂自荐。

sentences.en: And everybody, you know, they all fall for this.
sentences.zh: 然后每个人，你知道的，都上当了。

sentences.en: Oh, what a lovely idea.
sentences.zh: 哦，多么棒的主意啊。

sentences.en: What a kind man.
sentences.zh: 多么善良的人啊。

sentences.en: I mean, we're recording this today after the Trump inauguration,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们今天是特朗普就职典礼之后录制这期节目的，

sentences.en: where all these heads of tech companies that until Trump won the election were all over their mission being to spread happiness and joy and promote diversity and equity.
sentences.zh: 当时所有这些科技公司的巨头们，在特朗普赢得大选之前，到处宣扬他们的使命是传播幸福与快乐、促进多样性和平等。

sentences.en: And now they've binned all that.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们把这一切都扔进了垃圾桶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Very nakedly.
sentences.zh: 极其赤裸裸地。

sentences.en: Do you think that this is the first example of kind of avaricious corporations dressing up their greed behind a kind of show of piety?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是贪婪的企业用慈善的外表掩盖其贪婪的第一个例子吗？

sentences.en: It's got to be one of the first, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这肯定是最早的例子之一，对吧？

sentences.en: One of the early ones.
sentences.zh: 早期例子之一。

sentences.en: One of the most eye-catching early ones, definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是最引人注目的早期例子之一。

sentences.en: Because it is a brilliant manoeuvre.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个绝妙的策略。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是。

sentences.en: If you have global ambitions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有全球野心的话。

sentences.en: And all these people believe it.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些人居然都相信了。

sentences.en: They completely believe it.
sentences.zh: 他们完全相信了。

sentences.en: And here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键就在这里。

sentences.en: The International African Association, which sounds like it's a charity and which they have all endorsed, is actually a private company run by Leopold himself.
sentences.zh: 国际非洲协会听起来像是一个慈善机构，并且得到了他们所有人的背书，实际上是由利奥波德本人经营的私人公司。

sentences.en: For his benefit.
sentences.zh: 为了他的利益。

sentences.en: For his benefit.
sentences.zh: 为了他的利益。

sentences.en: So the only thing he doesn't have, actually, is the colony.
sentences.zh: 所以他唯一没有的东西，实际上就是殖民地。

sentences.en: You know, he's got the association, but he doesn't have the colony.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他有了协会，却没有殖民地。

sentences.en: And where is he going to get the colony?
sentences.zh: 那他要从哪里去弄到殖民地呢？

sentences.en: Well, the answer is from the one person who wasn't there at that meeting in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 答案是从唯一一个没有出席布鲁塞尔那场会议的人那里获得。

sentences.en: And this is the most famous of all African explorers.
sentences.zh: 这就是所有非洲探险家中最大名鼎鼎的那位。

sentences.en: We've already mentioned him.
sentences.zh: 我们已经提到过他了。

sentences.en: Henry Morton Stanley.
sentences.zh: 亨利·莫顿·斯坦利。

sentences.en: Now, we'll just sketch Stanley very briefly because he really is worthy of a Arrested History series in himself.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们简要概述一下斯坦利，因为他本身就完全值得做一期“被捕的历史”系列节目。

sentences.en: He had an amazing life, Stanley.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利度过了神奇的一生。

sentences.en: He was born in Wales in 1841 and he was born as John Rowland's bastard.
sentences.zh: 他于1841年出生于威尔士，出生时的名字叫约翰·罗兰兹的私生子。

sentences.en: He was the illegitimate son of a housemaid.
sentences.zh: 他是一个女佣的私生子。

sentences.en: That's the entry that is in the Book of Births.
sentences.zh: 这就是出生登记册上的记录。

sentences.en: He spends his childhood in a workhouse.
sentences.zh: 他在济贫院度过了童年。

sentences.en: He emigrates to New Orleans when he's 18 years old.
sentences.zh: 18岁时他移民到新奥尔良。

sentences.en: He fought for the Confederates.
sentences.zh: 他为南方邦联作战。

sentences.en: Then he fought for the Union.
sentences.zh: 然后他为北方联邦作战。

sentences.en: Then he joined the Union Navy.
sentences.zh: 接着他加入了联邦海军。

sentences.en: Then he renamed himself Henry Morton Stanley after a New Orleans businessman.
sentences.zh: 然后他随了一位新奥尔良商人的姓，将自己改名为亨利·莫顿·斯坦利。

sentences.en: And then he became a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 后来他成了一名记者。

sentences.en: And he went to the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 他去过奥斯曼帝国。

sentences.en: He went to Persia.
sentences.zh: 他去过波斯。

sentences.en: He went to the Crimea.
sentences.zh: 他去过克里米亚。

sentences.en: He went to Abyssinia with a British expedition.
sentences.zh: 他随英国探险队去过阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: But most famously, the New York Herald sent him to Central Africa to find Dr. Livingstone, which he did near Lake Tanganyika in 1871.
sentences.zh: 但最著名的是，《纽约先驱报》派他去中非寻找利文斯顿博士，他于1871年在坦噶尼喀湖附近找到了。

sentences.en: And then he invented, almost certainly invented, this fantastic line.
sentences.zh: 然后他发明了，几乎可以肯定是发明了这句精彩的台词。

sentences.en: So disappointing.
sentences.zh: 太让人失望了。

sentences.en: I know, it's disappointing.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这很令人失望。

sentences.en: Let's pretend that he said it.
sentences.zh: 我们就当他说过这句话吧。

sentences.en: Dr. Livingstone, I presume.
sentences.zh: 想必您就是利文斯顿博士吧。

sentences.en: When he met Livingstone, which flashed around the world and made him a household name, a genuine international celebrity.
sentences.zh: 当他与利文斯顿会面时，这句话传遍了全世界，使他家喻户晓，成为真正的国际名人。

sentences.en: And he writes it up in enormously long books, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他把这些写成了厚厚的大部头书，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实写了。

sentences.en: Which have great sellers.
sentences.zh: 这些书都非常畅销。

sentences.en: So he gets commissioned to write one book and he ends up writing three.
sentences.zh: 所以他原本只受委托写一本书，最后却写了三本。

sentences.en: That's very familiar.
sentences.zh: 这真是太熟悉了。

sentences.en: Nothing wrong with that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不对的，汤姆。

sentences.en: I commend that kind of behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我很赞赏这种行为。

sentences.en: Yeah, very familiar.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常熟悉。

sentences.en: So then he went on another expedition three years later,
sentences.zh: 三年后他又进行了另一次探险，

sentences.en: sent this time by the New York Herald and the Daily Telegraph in London to map the Great Lakes and to look for the source of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 这次是由伦敦的《纽约先驱报》和《每日电讯报》派遣，去绘制五大湖地图并寻找尼罗河的源头。

sentences.en: And that's where he's been during Leopold's conference.
sentences.zh: 这就是他在利奥波德开会期间一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: And he has begun that, hasn't he, on the east coast of Africa at Zanzibar.
sentences.zh: 他从非洲东海岸的桑给巴尔开始了那次探险，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's heading westwards.
sentences.zh: 他正向西进发。

sentences.en: And he wouldn't be the first European to have gone from east to west coast, but he is the first who does it basically by following the line of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 他不会是从东海岸到西海岸的第一位欧洲人，但他基本上是沿着刚果河的路线完成这一壮举的第一人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: An incredibly well-publicised journey, one that was followed by newspaper readers across the world as you would follow reports of great sporting fixtures or something.
sentences.zh: 这是一次宣传得极其到位的旅程，全世界的报纸读者都在关注它，就像关注重大体育赛事的报道一样。

sentences.en: Tremendous excitement.
sentences.zh: 令人无比兴奋。

sentences.en: In August 1877, Stanley reached the trading post of Boma, which is on the right bank of the Congo River near the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 1877年8月，斯坦利抵达了位于海岸附近刚果河右岸的博马贸易站。

sentences.en: An extraordinary, extraordinary achievement.
sentences.zh: 这是一次极其了不起的成就。

sentences.en: 7,000 miles, Tom, in three years, he did on foot.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他花了三年时间步行走了7000英里。

sentences.en: Now, Leopold has been following this with great intereSt.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德一直对此保持着浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.zh: 他的确这么做了。

sentences.en: The kind of looting of his people.
sentences.zh: 关于对他人民的一种掠夺。

sentences.en: So I would guess from that that probably they're not thrilled about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我由此推测，他们大概对此很不高兴。

sentences.en: No, he wrote to the Portuguese king and he said, you're taking too many slaves, there's nobody left.
sentences.zh: 不，他写信给葡萄牙国王说，你们抓了太多奴隶，都没人了。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese king actually wrote back to him, sent him a letter and said, I've heard there's loads of people in the Congo.
sentences.zh: 而葡萄牙国王居然回信给他，给他寄了一封信说，我听说刚果有的是人。

sentences.en: What are you complaining about?
sentences.zh: 你在抱怨什么？

sentences.en: Shut up.
sentences.zh: 闭嘴吧。

sentences.en: And that was the extent of this meeting of minds between these two kings.
sentences.zh: 这就是这两位国王之间思想交流的全部程度。

sentences.en: In the years that followed, the Congo became prey to all kinds of inroads in the Portuguese, the Spanish, the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几年里，刚果成了葡萄牙人、西班牙人、荷兰人各种侵略掠夺的牺牲品。

sentences.en: There's lots of factualism, the civil wars, and basically the kingdom falls apart.
sentences.zh: 这里有许多派系之争、内战，基本上王国分崩离析了。

sentences.en: But much of this is a mystery to Europeans.
sentences.zh: 但对欧洲人来说，其中大部分仍然是个谜。

sentences.en: Europeans can't get into the interior.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人无法进入内陆。

sentences.en: They know that the Congo River is a vast river.
sentences.zh: 他们知道刚果河是一条巨大的河流。

sentences.en: It's the second largest river in Africa, third largest by volume in the world.
sentences.zh: 它是非洲第二大河，按水量计算是世界第三大河。

sentences.en: But they can't go up it because once you start to go upstream, once you go up river, very quickly the river gives way to 200 miles worth of rapids and gorges and canyons and so on.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法逆流而上，因为一旦你开始逆流而上，往河的上游走，河道很快就会变成长达200英里的急流、峡谷和深谷等等。

sentences.en: So you have to get out of your ship and walk.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须下船步行。

sentences.en: And at that point, it's very rocky terrain, what's called the Crystal Mountains.
sentences.zh: 而且在那一带，地形非常崎岖，被称为水晶山脉。

sentences.en: And Europeans, as soon as they started to do that, they would get malaria or yellow fever and they'd basically all die.
sentences.zh: 而欧洲人一旦开始这么做，就会染上疟疾或黄热病，基本上全都会丧命。

sentences.en: Dominic, there is a British expedition in 1816.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，1816年有过一次英国探险。

sentences.en: There is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: Led by a Royal Navy captain who describes the scenery as beautiful and not inferior to any on the banks of the Thames.
sentences.zh: 由一名英国皇家海军船长率领，他将那里的风景描述为美丽迷人，不逊色于泰晤士河岸的任何风景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which is obviously the highest praise.
sentences.zh: 这显然是极高的赞誉。

sentences.en: The highest, the very highest praise.
sentences.zh: 极高，非常极高的赞誉。

sentences.en: The Englishman could possibly give any river.
sentences.zh: 英国人对任何河流所能给出的最高赞誉。

sentences.en: But he's a good example.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: He only gets a little bit of the way and then they basically have to go back.
sentences.zh: 他只走了一小段路，然后基本上就不得不返回了。

sentences.en: They have to go back because they were all horribly ill.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不返回，因为所有人都病得不轻。

sentences.en: So even in the 1870s, the vast basin of the Congo, we're talking about one and a half million square miles of territory.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在1870年代，广袤的刚果盆地，我们谈论的是一百五十万平方英里的领土。

sentences.en: That's about what, the size of India?
sentences.zh: 那大概有多大，差不多有印度那么大吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's a massive, massive stretch of land and home to, now this is very controversial, but let us say somewhere between roughly 8 and 12 million people.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一片极其广袤的土地，现在这里居住着——这很有争议，但我们姑且认为是大约800万到1200万人。

sentences.en: It is almost completely unknown to Europeans.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人对这里几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: They still talk about the blank space on the map, an empty space on the map, which is, of course, quite wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在谈论地图上的空白处，地图上的空白区域，当然，这大错特错。

sentences.en: Now, Stanley has been through it, but not all of it.
sentences.zh: 现在，斯坦利已经穿过了这里，但不是全部。

sentences.en: Stanley had tracked the river for about 1,500 miles.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利追踪这条河大约走了1500英里。

sentences.en: So that's only about half the length of the Congo River.
sentences.zh: 所以这大约只占刚果河长度的一半。

sentences.en: And he's only had limited interactions with the locals, but he does know two crucial things, which he's able to tell Leopold that day in the palace.
sentences.zh: 而且他与当地人的接触有限，但他确实知道两件至关重要的事情，这使他那天能在宫殿里告诉利奥波德。

sentences.en: First of all, the people of the Congo, they don't have anything like the military technology to resist a European takeover.
sentences.zh: 首先，刚果人民没有任何军事技术来抵御欧洲人的接管。

sentences.en: It's a myth that they're completely unsophisticated.
sentences.zh: 说他们完全没有文化，这是一个神话。

sentences.en: They have brilliant pottery, they're brilliant woodworkers and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们有精美的陶器，他们是出色的木工，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But in terms of weapons, they only have spears and arrows and some very ancient Portuguese muskets.
sentences.zh: 但在武器方面，他们只有长矛、弓箭和一些非常古老的葡萄牙滑膛枪。

sentences.en: So, you know, an invading European force would be able to wipe the floor with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，一支入侵的欧洲军队可以把他们打得落花流水。

sentences.en: And the second thing, even more important, there is no one powerful state in the Congo Basin.
sentences.zh: 第二点，甚至更重要，刚果盆地没有一个强大的国家。

sentences.en: There are more than 200 different ethnic groups.
sentences.zh: 这里有200多个不同的民族。

sentences.en: They speak 400 different languages and dialects.
sentences.zh: 他们说着400种不同的语言和方言。

sentences.en: There's a massive variety.
sentences.zh: 这里有巨大的多样性。

sentences.en: So some of them are Higmas who live in the forests and some of them are more settled farming peoples who live on the savannas.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些是住在森林里的希格马人，另一些是住在稀树草原上更加定居的农耕民族。

sentences.en: But they're very fragmented.
sentences.zh: 但他们非常分散。

sentences.en: They're always fighting each other.
sentences.zh: 他们总是在互相征战。

sentences.en: It's a little bit like, you know, when Cortez arrived in Mesoamerica and found there were all kinds of rivalries and things that he could exploit.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，你知道的，当科尔特斯抵达中美洲时，发现那里有各种各样的敌对势力和可以利用的东西。

sentences.en: But there isn't an equivalent of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 但这里没有阿兹特克人的同类。

sentences.en: There's no equivalent of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 没有阿兹特克人的同类。

sentences.en: There's no equivalent of that.
sentences.zh: 没有那种同类。

sentences.en: So it's even better than that.
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至比那还要好。

sentences.en: For a European predator, the people of the Congo are the perfect prey.
sentences.zh: 对于欧洲掠夺者来说，刚果人民是完美的猎物。

sentences.en: And Dominic, isn't there one other factor that Stanley has discovered by going along the river, which is that if you can get past the rapids up kind of into the highlands,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，难道斯坦利沿着河流探索还发现了另一个因素吗？那就是如果你能穿过急流进入高原，

sentences.en: then the Congo is very, very navigable.
sentences.zh: 那么刚果河就非常非常适合通航。

sentences.en: And there are all these kind of tributaries.
sentences.zh: 而且有所有这些各种各样的支流。

sentences.en: So there are thousands and thousands of miles of navigable water.
sentences.zh: 所以有成千上万英里的通航水域。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like, you know, railways have been laid or something.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像，你知道的，铁路已经铺好了一样。

sentences.en: If you can just get your steamboat up past these rapids, then you can use the river to go very, very deep into the Congo.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把你的汽船开过这些急流，那么你就可以利用这条河深入刚果腹地。

sentences.en: And if there is raw material, say ivory or perhaps in Dukov's rubber, then you can use it to bring it back.
sentences.zh: 如果那里有原材料，比方说象牙，或者在杜科夫的故事里的橡胶，那么你就可以用它运回来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, there are the lineaments of your transport infrastructure right there waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你的交通基础设施的轮廓就在那里等着你。

sentences.en: So for Leopold, all of this is absolutely great news.
sentences.zh: 所以对利奥波德来说，所有这些绝对都是好消息。

sentences.en: He seems to have hit it off with Stanley straight away.
sentences.zh: 他似乎立刻就和斯坦利合得来了。

sentences.en: Leopold spoke perfect English, despite his enormous nose and his gangling awkwardness.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德说一口流利的英语，尽管他有着巨大的鼻子和笨拙的体态。

sentences.en: He can be charming when he wants to and he flatters Stanley.
sentences.zh: 只要他愿意，他可以很有魅力，并且他奉承了斯坦利。

sentences.en: Stanley, of course, is desperate for flattery because he hasn't had it in London.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利当然极度渴望奉承，因为他在伦敦没有得到过。

sentences.en: And that autumn, 1878, Leopold says, I'd like to offer you a five-year contract.
sentences.zh: 1878年那个秋天，利奥波德说：“我想为你提供一份五年的合同。”

sentences.en: For every year you spend in Africa, I will pay you 50,000 francs.
sentences.zh: 你在非洲度过的每一年，我都会付给你5万法郎。

sentences.en: And I will pay for an expeditionary force to go with you up the Congo.
sentences.zh: 我将资助一支远征军和你一起逆刚果河而上。

sentences.en: So in terms of Stanley's earnings, in today's money, Leopold is effectively offering him two million pounds, a lot of money for a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 所以就斯坦利的收入而言，以今天的金钱计算，利奥波德实际上是在向他提供200万英镑，对一个记者来说这是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And so he's buying Stanley's knowledge, presumably.
sentences.zh: 所以他大概是在买斯坦利的知识。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But is he also buying Stanley's prestige as the man who knows the Congo?
sentences.zh: 但他也买下了斯坦利作为深谙刚果之人的声望吗？

sentences.en: The sense that if he's got Stanley with him, then the project must be a realistic one.
sentences.zh: 那种如果他带着斯坦利，那么这个项目一定是一个现实的项目的印象。

sentences.en: It must be a serious one.
sentences.zh: 这一定是一个严肃的项目。

sentences.en: I think he's buying three things, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为他买下了三样东西。

sentences.en: So I think he's buying Stanley's knowledge.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他在买斯坦利的知识。

sentences.en: Stanley knows he's gone along the river.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利知道，他曾沿着这条河走过。

sentences.en: Number two, I do think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 第二点，我确实认为你完全说对了。

sentences.en: He's buying the prestige and the celebrity.
sentences.zh: 他在买声望和名气。

sentences.en: Stanley will become the face of this charitable expedition.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利将成为这次慈善远征的代言人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the third thing is he's genuinely buying Stanley's.
sentences.zh: 但第三件事是，他真正买下的是斯坦利的……

sentences.en: You know, Stanley is going to have to do the work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，斯坦利将不得不干活。

sentences.en: He's going to have to put the work in on the ground.
sentences.zh: 他必须在实地付出努力。

sentences.en: Now, Leopold knows that Stanley is a hard worker and he drives other people very hard.
sentences.zh: 现在，利奥波德知道斯坦利是一个工作刻苦的人，他对其他人也要求极严。

sentences.en: He says to Stanley, what I want you to do, I want you to establish a station at the mouth of the Congo that will be our big base.
sentences.zh: 他对斯坦利说：“我希望你做的是，在刚果河口建立一个据点，这将是我们的主要基地。”

sentences.en: Then, and this will be a really important thing, build a road or indeed a railway around these rapids, through these mountains.
sentences.zh: 然后，这将是一件非常重要的事情，围绕这些急流，穿过这些山脉，修建一条公路甚至是一条铁路。

sentences.en: And basically what I want you to do, start with the road and get porters to carry disassembled steamboats through this territory to the other side of the rapids, 200 miles,
sentences.zh: 基本上我希望你做的，是从修建公路开始，让搬运工把拆卸开的汽船通过这片领土运到急流的另一侧，即200英里外，

sentences.en: then reassemble the steamboats and then head up river on the steamboats for a thousand miles, establishing trading posts and stations and whatnot as you go.
sentences.zh: 然后重新组装汽船，接着乘汽船逆流而上飞行一千英里，一路上建立贸易站和据点之类的东西。

sentences.en: So this is a pretty big operation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次规模相当大的行动。

sentences.en: Stanley says, fine.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利说，好吧。

sentences.en: Now, the fine point of this contract is deliberately ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 现在，这份合同的微观细节是刻意含糊不清的。

sentences.en: The contract leaves it very unclear who Stanley is working for.
sentences.zh: 合同非常不明确地指出斯坦利究竟在为谁工作。

sentences.en: Is he working for Leopold himself?
sentences.zh: 他是为利奥波德本人工作吗？

sentences.en: Is he working for the International African Association?
sentences.zh: 他是为国际非洲协会工作吗？

sentences.en: Or is he working for yet another organization called the Committee for Studies of the Upper Congo, which is another of Leopold's front organizations that he has set up?
sentences.zh: 还是他在为另一个名为上刚果研究委员会的组织工作？这是利奥波德设立的又一个傀儡组织之一。

sentences.en: And Stanley must have known that something was a bit off about this because he demands, he says, I must have all the money up front.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利一定知道这其中有点不对劲，因为他要求，他说：“我必须预支所有的资金。”

sentences.en: And this plan to use porters to carry bits of steamship up to the Congo.
sentences.zh: 而这个使用搬运工将轮船零件运到刚果的计划。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, presumably that will require a fair degree of force.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这大概需要相当程度的武力。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So is Stanley knowingly buying into that?
sentences.zh: 那么斯坦利是在明知情的情况下接受这一点的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Because Stanley had employed porters on his previous journeys and that had often involved a degree of payment, but also a degree of force as well.
sentences.zh: 因为斯坦利在他先前的旅程中曾雇用过搬运工，这通常涉及一定程度的报酬，但也在一定程度上伴随着武力。

sentences.en: But to carry a steamship is a different business from carrying, you know, supplies or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但运送一艘轮船与运送，你知道的，补给品或其他东西是不同的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a pretty military operation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一次相当具有军事性质的行动。

sentences.en: But remember, Leopold has promised he will pay for an expeditionary force, basically a mercenary force, to go upriver with Stanley.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，利奥波德已经承诺，他将支付一支远征军的费用，基本上是一支雇佣军部队，与斯坦利一起逆流而上。

sentences.en: But just to be clear, Stanley is walking into this with his eyes wide open.
sentences.zh: 但直白地说，斯坦利是在睁大眼睛跳进这个火坑的。

sentences.en: Oh, his eyes are definitely open.
sentences.zh: 哦，他的眼睛绝对是睁开的。

sentences.en: And his subordinates, they have to sign the equivalent of non-disclosure agreements.
sentences.zh: 而且他的下属，他们必须签署相当于保密协议的文件。

sentences.en: They have to sign strict confidentiality clauses.
sentences.zh: 他们必须签署严格的保密条款。

sentences.en: They can't tell anybody about what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们不能对任何人透露他们在做什么。

sentences.en: Again, a pretty dodgy sign, I would say.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是一个相当可疑的信号，我得说。

sentences.en: Now, Leopold, of course, he wants to hide this from foreign competitors.
sentences.zh: 现在，利奥波德当然想对外国竞争对手隐瞒这一点。

sentences.en: He's paranoid that the Germans or the French will get in on the act.
sentences.zh: 他患有被迫害妄想症，担心德国人或法国人会插手。

sentences.en: But he also wants to hide this from his own people.
sentences.zh: 但他也想对自己的国民隐瞒这一点。

sentences.en: Because remember, here's the really remarkable thing.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，这里最了不起的事情是，

sentences.en: Unlike some of the rest of the scramble of Africa, this is not being done for Belgium.
sentences.zh: 与瓜分非洲的其他一些行动不同，这不是为了比利时而做的。

sentences.en: It's not been done for the people or the government of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 这不是为了比利时人民或比利时政府而做的。

sentences.en: It's being done for one man, King Leopold.
sentences.zh: 这是为了一个人，利奥波德国王而做的。

sentences.en: And that's what makes it different.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的不同之处。

sentences.en: So, February 1879.
Stanley sets off.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利出发了。

sentences.en: And as part of the confidentiality, he travels under an alias.
sentences.zh: 作为保密工作的一部分，他使用化名旅行。

sentences.en: He calls himself Monsieur Henri.
sentences.zh: 他自称亨利先生。

sentences.en: So, Monsieur Henri goes off to Africa.
sentences.zh: 于是，亨利先生出发前往非洲。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in Belgium, Leopold has set up yet another organization, another front group, called the International Association of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，回到比利时，利奥波德又建立了一个组织，另一个名为刚果国际协会的傀儡集团。

sentences.en: Now, this, people may have lost track at this point of all the different associations.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们此时可能已经记不清所有这些不同的协会了。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 这就是重点所在。

sentences.en: That's what Leopold wants you to do.
sentences.zh: 这正是利奥波德希望你做的。

sentences.en: Because the names are all vaguely similar.
sentences.zh: 因为这些名字都模棱两可地相似。

sentences.en: They're very similar.
sentences.zh: 它们非常相似。

sentences.en: He wants you to think that this is the International African Association set up at his conference.
sentences.zh: 他想让你认为这是在他的会议上成立的国际非洲协会。

sentences.en: And that's a charitable one.
sentences.zh: 那是一个慈善机构。

sentences.en: A charitable one, because it has the same flag, the same iconography.
sentences.zh: 一个慈善机构，因为它有着相同的旗帜，相同的图标。

sentences.en: The flag is blue with the gold star.
sentences.zh: 国旗是蓝色底上有金色星星。

sentences.en: But this one is answerable just to him, the International Association of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 但这个只对标他一个人，即刚果国际协会。

sentences.en: And this is the organization that he intends will run his new fiefdom.
sentences.zh: 这就是他打算用来管理他的新封地的组织。

sentences.en: It's like if you set up a very sinister, exploitative organization called Oxfim.
sentences.zh: 这就好比你建立了一个非常阴险、极具剥削性的组织，却叫它“乐施会”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly.

sentences.zh: 这就是后来的布拉柴维尔，如今它是前法国刚果共和国的首都。

sentences.en: So a rival Congolese territory.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个竞争对手的刚果领地。

sentences.en: And there's a massive media row between Stanley and Braza.
sentences.zh: 史丹利和布拉萨之间爆发了巨大的媒体口水战。

sentences.en: The Portuguese hear about this and the Portuguese say, what?
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人听到这个消息后说，什么？

sentences.en: We were the first to the Congo.
sentences.zh: 我们才是最先到达刚果的。

sentences.en: What's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Get out.
sentences.zh: 滚开。

sentences.en: And the British say, well, if there's any dispute about this, we would really much prefer that the Portuguese have the Congo.
sentences.zh: 而英国人则说，好吧，如果对此有什么争议，我们其实更愿意让葡萄牙人拥有刚果。

sentences.en: So this is a problem for Leopold.
sentences.zh: 所以这对利奥波德来说是个问题。

sentences.en: He needs somebody to back him.
sentences.zh: 他需要有人支持他。

sentences.en: And he does something here very clever.
sentences.zh: 他在这里做了一件非常聪明的事。

sentences.en: He goes outside Europe to another relatively new country like Belgium and another country that has a history of signing treaties with indigenous peoples.
sentences.zh: 他走出了欧洲，去找另一个像比利时一样相对年轻的国家，另一个有与原住民签署条约历史的国家。

sentences.en: Slightly one-sided treaties, some people might say, that end up not being worth the paper they're written on.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会说，那是稍微有些不平等的条约，最后往往成了一纸空文。

sentences.en: But complemented by a love of liberty.
sentences.zh: 但辅以对自由的热爱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this country is, of course, the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 这个国家当然就是美利坚合众国。

sentences.en: And he has the perfect intermediary.
sentences.zh: 他拥有完美的中间人。

sentences.en: Another Dickensian character called Henry Shelton Sanford, who had previously been the American ambassador to Brussels.
sentences.zh: 另一个充满狄更斯色彩的人物叫亨利·谢尔顿·桑福德，他曾担任美国驻布鲁塞尔大使。

sentences.en: And Henry Shelton Sanford, if you look him up, he's got a big stovepipe hat.
sentences.zh: 如果你去查查亨利·谢尔顿·桑福德，他戴着一顶高筒礼帽。

sentences.en: He's got the moustache.
sentences.zh: 留着八字胡。

sentences.en: He's got the kind of gold, pince-nez glasses.
sentences.zh: 他戴着那种金色、带夹鼻的眼镜。

sentences.en: And he's got the title general, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他顶着将军的头衔，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, fake.
sentences.zh: 对，是假的。

sentences.en: He got given because he donated artillery or something to the Union during the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 这个头衔是因为他在内战期间向联邦捐赠了火炮什么的而授予他的。

sentences.en: And he uses it all the time, but it's completely bogus.
sentences.zh: 他一直拿着这个头衔招摇撞骗，但完全是假的。

sentences.en: He's a fake general.
sentences.zh: 他是个假将军。

sentences.en: I mean, he's perfect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他太完美了。

sentences.en: And he's a massive investor in Florida.
sentences.zh: 而且他是佛罗里达的大投资者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's lost loads of money in Florida, Florida railroads.
sentences.zh: 他在佛罗里达赔了巨资，全赔在佛罗里达的铁路上了。

sentences.en: So he needs money, which makes him the perfect pawn for Leopold.
sentences.zh: 所以他需要钱，这使他成为利奥波德的完美棋子。

sentences.en: He needs a rich friend.
sentences.zh: 他需要一个有钱的朋友。

sentences.en: Leopold sends him to Washington with a personal letter to the Republican president, Chester Arthur.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德把他派往华盛顿，带着一封给共和党总统切斯特·阿瑟的亲笔信。

sentences.en: And Leopold says, I'm setting up this colony in the Congo.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德说，我要在刚果建立这个殖民地。

sentences.en: And really, it's about two things.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，这关乎两件事。

sentences.en: It's about fighting slavery and about free trade.
sentences.zh: 一是为了反抗奴隶制，二是为了自由贸易。

sentences.en: And as it happens, Arthur is a Republican.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，阿瑟是一位共和党人。

sentences.en: And that's basically what the Republican Party in the 1870s and 1880s stands for.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是十九世纪七八十年代共和党的主张。

sentences.en: Arthur says, oh, my God, this sounds absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 阿瑟说，噢，天哪，这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: And so in April 1884, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 于是在1884年4月，美国

sentences.en: State Department issues the very first official recognition of Leopold's colony.
sentences.zh: 国务院对利奥波德的殖民地发出了第一份官方承认。

sentences.en: And they don't understand what it is because at this stage...
sentences.zh: 他们根本不明白这是什么，因为在这个阶段……

sentences.en: Because they think it's going to be like the United States, only in Africa.
sentences.zh: 因为他们以为这会像美国一样，只不过是在非洲。

sentences.en: They absolutely think it's going to be the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对以为这里会变成美国。

sentences.en: And what is worse, in the official statement, they muddle up the International Association of the Congo and the International African Association.
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，他们在官方声明中把刚果国际协会和国际非洲协会搞混了。

sentences.en: They use both names within about three sentences.
sentences.zh: 他们在差不多三句话里同时使用了这两个名字。

sentences.en: And of course, that's exactly what Leopold wanted.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是利奥波德想要的。

sentences.en: That was why he did it, because he wants everybody to be confused.
sentences.zh: 这就是他这么做的原因，因为他想让所有人都糊涂。

sentences.en: He is cunning, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他很狡猾，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is a fox.
sentences.zh: 他简直就是个老狐狸。

sentences.en: He is a fox.
sentences.zh: 他就是个老狐狸。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, when the Americans have recognized it, the French are the next to get on board.
sentences.zh: 现在，在这个时候，当美国人承认了之后，法国人成了下一个加入的。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because even though they wanted it themselves, they become paranoid that Leopold is going to run out of money and sell it to the British.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管他们自己也想要，但他们开始患得患失，担心利奥波德会花光钱然后把这卖给英国人。

sentences.en: And is that because of Stanley?
sentences.zh: 是因为斯坦利吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The Stanley would be the intermediary.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利将充当中间人。

sentences.en: Hanging out in London and everything.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦到处晃悠之类的。

sentences.en: And that is the last thing they want.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们最不愿意看到的。

sentences.en: And also, the French don't need to feel intimidated by Belgium, do they?
sentences.zh: 而且，法国人没必要对比利时感到畏惧，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I guess not.
sentences.zh: 不，我想是的。

sentences.en: I guess not.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: And they kind of are still thinking, well, if the Belgians get it, at least it's not the Germans.
sentences.zh: 而且他们心里还在想，好吧，如果比利时人得到了它，至少不是德国人。

sentences.en: Next are the Germans.
sentences.zh: 接下来是德国人。

sentences.en: Now, Bismarck, the Chancellor of Germany, the great statesman of Germany, he sees through Leopold, I think, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 现在，德国首相俾斯麦，德国伟大的政治家，我觉得他有点看穿了利奥波德。

sentences.en: Because on the documents that he gets, he writes the words swindle and fantasies.
sentences.zh: 因为他在收到的文件上写下了“骗局”和“幻想”这两个词。

sentences.en: And he's not wrong, is he?
sentences.zh: 他可没说错，对吧？

sentences.en: But Bismarck thinks, I don't want the French to get the Congo or Britain.
sentences.zh: 但俾斯麦想，我可不想让法国人或者英国人得到刚果。

sentences.en: So maybe if little Belgium gets it, yeah, fine.
sentences.zh: 所以如果让小小的比利时得到它，好吧，也行。

sentences.en: And it's the weakness of Belgium that Leopold is basically leveraging.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德基本上就是利用了比利时的弱小。

sentences.en: Even though Belgium is not going to get it.
sentences.zh: 尽管比利时根本不会得到它。

sentences.en: But Leopold himself, that's the great irony of all this.
sentences.zh: 但利奥波德本人，这才是这一切中最巨大的讽刺。

sentences.en: All this comes to a head at the conference in Berlin that opens at the end of 1884.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切在1884年底开幕的柏林会议上达到了顶点。

sentences.en: So this is the great conference that marks the sort of high point.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那场标志着某种顶峰的伟大会议。

sentences.en: The Israeli and the scramble for Bismarck.
sentences.zh: 对俾斯麦而言的以色列和列强争夺。

sentences.en: And there are delegates from America, from Russia, from the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 那里有来自美国、俄国、奥斯曼帝国的代表。

sentences.en: Of course, no Africans deciding their own destiny.
sentences.zh: 当然，没有非洲人来决定他们自己的命运。

sentences.en: Nobody thinks that would be remotely appropriate.
sentences.zh: 没有人会觉得这有什么不妥。

sentences.en: Now, actually, Stanley is there as an advisor to the American delegation.
sentences.zh: 实际上，斯坦利是以美国代表团顾问的身份出席的。

sentences.en: And it says something that Stanley himself feels a little bit queasy about this spectacle.
sentences.zh: 这说明了一点，即斯坦利本人对这种场面也感到有点反胃。

sentences.en: He says that the sight of all the delegates rushing to carve up Africa reminded him of when he was on an expedition and they would kill some sort of beaSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，看到所有代表争先恐后地瓜分非洲，让他想起他以前在远征时，他们会杀死某种野兽。

sentences.en: And he says, my porters, you know, they would rush with gleaming knives for slaughtered game.
sentences.zh: 他说，我的搬运工们，你知道的，他们会拿着寒光闪闪的刀子扑向被宰杀的猎物。

sentences.en: And that's what these delegates are like.
sentences.zh: 这些代表们就是这个样子的。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose to hack off the ivory.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我猜是为了砍下象牙。

sentences.en: To hack off the ivory.
sentences.zh: 为了砍下象牙。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The tusks.
sentences.zh: 象牙。

sentences.en: So by February 1885, the conference has reached an agreement.
sentences.zh: 因此到1885年2月，会议达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: And for Leopold, it is the perfect result.
sentences.zh: 对利奥波德来说，这是最完美的结局。

sentences.en: It's a total triumph.
sentences.zh: 这是一场彻底的胜利。

sentences.en: All the powers agree that they will recognize the International Congo Association as the owner of almost all of the Congo Basin.
sentences.zh: 所有列强都同意承认刚果国际协会为几乎整个刚果盆地的所有者。

sentences.en: And that's the dodgy one, not the humanitarian one.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个靠不住的，而不是人道主义的那个。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The dodgy one.
sentences.zh: 那个靠不住的。

sentences.en: Leopold's private company.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德的私人公司。

sentences.en: So he has got a territory 76 times the size of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有了一片面积是比利时76倍的领土。

sentences.en: And it will belong not to Belgium, but to Leopold personally.
sentences.zh: 这片土地不属于比利时，而是属于利奥波德个人。

sentences.en: So at last he has the fiefdom he wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以他终于得到了他梦寐以求的封地。

sentences.en: And three months later, in May 1885, he drops all the fiction.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，即1885年5月，他抛弃了所有的伪装。

sentences.en: The International Congo Association is allowed to lapse.
sentences.zh: 刚果国际协会被允许失效。

sentences.en: The only thing that remains of it is its flag, the blue flag with the gold star.
sentences.zh: 唯一保留下来的只有它的旗帜，那面带有金色星星的蓝底旗帜。

sentences.en: And on the 29th of May, by royal decree, its lands, this huge stretch of territory, is renamed the Etat Indépendant du Congo, the Free State of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 5月29日，通过皇家法令，它的土地，这片巨大的广袤领土，被重新命名为刚果自由国（Etat Indépendant du Congo）。

sentences.en: And Leopold is named as its founding sovereign.
sentences.zh: 利奥波德被指定为其创始君主。

sentences.en: He kind of briefly considered calling himself Emperor of the Congo, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他曾短暂考虑过自称为刚果皇帝，对吧？

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实想过。

sentences.en: And giving all the various chieftains who'd signed treaties with him outfits modelled on the uniforms of the beef eaters.
sentences.zh: 并给所有曾与他签署条约的各部落酋长发定制服装，款式仿照伦敦塔卫士的制服。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Be very hot.
sentences.zh: 会非常热。

sentences.en: Very sensible wearing.
sentences.zh: 穿起来非常明智。

sentences.en: In appropriate garments of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 穿着适合刚果的服装。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 但现在刚果自由国已经建立，利奥波德成为其君主，对于刚果人民来说，真正的噩梦开始了。

sentences.en: The horror, the horror, one might almost say.
